question: For one season only, 1887, walks counted as hits. St. Louis Browns slugger Tip O'Neill took full advantage. What batting average was he credited with at the time?
question_short: In 1887, walks counted as hits. What average was Tip O'Neill credited with?
answer_detail: The walks-as-hits rule lasted just that one season. When record-keepers stripped the walks back out in 1969, O'Neill's official mark fell to .435, still one of the highest single-season averages in big-league history.
answer_short: The rule lasted one season. Without the walks, his official average is .435.
